extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, publicists, communications/marketing teams who write press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for writing and placing calls-to-action (CTAs) inside news/press releases so readers convert interest into measurable actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Directness
rubrics_metrics.description: Be direct about the action wanted; ambiguity causes friction; one primary CTA per release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State exactly what you want the reader to do (avoid vague phrasing). Limit to a single primary CTA to reduce choice friction; supporting CTAs may be secondary but should not compete with the main action.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTA Placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically at the end of the main body; some recommend 2-3 CTAs spaced throughout (beginning hook, mid-content reinforcement, end as final prompt); don't put primary CTA before key facts established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the primary CTA when the reader has enough information to decide (end of the main body is standard). If using multiple CTAs, space them (intro, mid, end) so they reinforce rather than distract; never put the primary ask before essential facts or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action-Oriented Language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer verbs that drive behavior: 'Subscribe', 'Buy Now', 'Register', 'Download', 'Learn More', 'Read the Report', 'Schedule a Demo', 'Join the Webinar'. Action verbs reduce ambiguity and increase click-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose-aligned CTA Wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Match CTA wording to the release's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples by purpose: Awareness -> 'Learn more' or 'Read more'; Lead generation -> 'Request demo' or 'Sign up'; Sales -> 'Buy now' or 'Order today'; Event -> 'Register' or 'RSVP'; Research -> 'Download the report'. Choose the CTA that fits the intended conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create Urgency / Scarcity When Appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: For product launches, promotions, services - create scarcity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use urgency/scarcity phrases to increase conversion where appropriate: 'Limited time', 'First 100 customers', 'Available through [date]'. Reserve urgency for real, verifiable constraints to avoid undermining credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a Destination (URL or Contact)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every CTA should give a clear destination the reader can reach (link or contact). Examples: 'Get the full report at [URL]'; 'Schedule a media interview by contacting [PR CONTACT]'. Use trackable URLs/UTMs when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable / Trackable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design CTAs so their performance can be measured (clicks, form submissions, downloads). Use unique links, UTM parameters, dedicated landing pages, or trackable contact routes to evaluate CTA effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity (Avoid Vague CTAs)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fuzzy CTAs like 'Find out more' without context. Be explicit about what the user will get (e.g., 'Download the 2026 market report') so expectations are set and conversions are higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete CTA Examples / Templates for News Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Example phrasings to use in news releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ready templates as models: 'Learn more about how [KEY FINDINGS] impact you, visit [LINK]'; 'Get the full report at [URL]'; 'Schedule a media interview by contacting [PR CONTACT]'. These illustrate destination, specificity, and actionable language.
